Resolves #18365

Related: #5822 · #18354 · #18360

The readiness poll can observe the Monaco addon namespace before its instance creates the editor registry. Guarding the registry lookup makes that state return false so polling continues. A ready editor still succeeds, and genuine editor-method exceptions still propagate.

Evidence: L3 (the existing real Neo wrapper browser cases plus isolated callback-state controls) → L3 required (AC-3). Residual: none.

Micro-review eligible: contained — one optional-chain correction in the existing test predicate.

## AC Evidence

| AC | Evidence |
|---|---|
| AC-1 | Outside CI: evaluated the exact callback with absent addon, namespace-before-registry, empty registry and ready editor; results below. |
| AC-2 | Outside CI: a ready editor whose getModel throws still propagates the original Error. |
| AC-3 | CI-covered: the six existing cases in test/playwright/component/wrapper/MonacoEditor.spec.mjs; locally passed using playwright.config.component.mjs. |

## Deltas from ticket

None substantive.

## Test Evidence

The exact page.evaluate callback was read from the spec and executed with controlled addon states:

| State | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Addon absent | false | false |
| Namespace exists, registry absent | TypeError | false |
| Empty registry | false | false |
| Ready editor with model | true | true |
| Existing getModel throws | original Error | original Error |

The before failure matches the exception in [the reported component job](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/actions/runs/33973844177/job/101328008490).

# PR Micro-Review

**Class:** mechanical — test-only, behaviour-preserving, one optional-chain in a poll predicate. No architectural concept, no consumed contract, no never-zone.

**Verdict:** Approved

**Glance:** Verified at `cd43759bf5`. The ticket says *"the addon namespace can exist before its editor registry does"*, and I went looking for **why**, because `map = {}` is an instance field on `Neo.main.addon.MonacoEditor` — a constructed instance always has it, so the stated premise is not obviously reachable. It is, and the mechanism is sharper than the ticket puts it: `Neo.setupClass` → `gatekeep` assigns the **class** to the namespace (`parentNs[className] = module`, `Neo.mjs:521`), and only later does `Main#registerAddon` (`Main.mjs:572-587`) run `Neo.create` + `Neo.applyToGlobalNs` to replace it with the instance. Between import and registration the namespace holds the **class**, which has neither `map` (instance field) nor `isReady` (instance config). `addon?.map[id]` therefore throws in exactly that window — not on a half-built instance, but on a class object. So the premise holds for a better reason than "the registry lags".

The fix is correct across all four states the ACs name: absent addon → `addon?.isReady` undefined → `false`; class-on-namespace → `map` undefined → `?.[id]` undefined → `false`; empty registry → `false`; ready editor+model → `true`. AC-2 holds by construction — no `catch` was added, so a genuine `getModel()` throw still propagates. Worth noting the throw was at the `const` initialiser, not in the returned predicate, which is why guarding the index is the minimal repair rather than reordering the expression.

**Bounded repair — confirmed, and the check was not free.** The prescription named `expectEditor` only, and exactly one line changed. The spec holds nine further unguarded `Neo.main.addon.MonacoEditor.map[id]` reads (`:104`, `:113`, `:136`, `:154`, `:163`, `:175`, `:185`, `:191`, `:223`), and I checked whether the repair left siblings exposed. It did not: every one is sequenced after an `expectEditor` gate that establishes readiness first — including `:223`, which sits three lines below an `await expectEditor(page)` in the very test that asserts `isReady === false` earlier on. Correct by sequence, not by luck, and not this PR's to widen. `git grep` finds no remaining `addon?.map[` anywhere in `src/` or `test/`.

The one thing I looked for and did not find: a state in which the guard could make the poll report ready *prematurely*. It cannot — `isReady` is an instance config, so the class object cannot answer it truthy, and the added `?.` only ever converts a throw into `false`, which the bounded `expect.poll` already handles.

Prior art worth linking rather than re-deriving: the same class of race — a consumer touching `Neo.main.addon.*` before registration completes — was fixed once at the App Worker proxy layer in `#7815` by awaiting addon `ready()` in `onDomContentLoaded`. Different reader (main realm vs worker proxy), same shape. Not a duplicate, and no reason to reopen it.

CI 16/16 green at head, which covers the component job and therefore AC-3's six real cases; I did not rerun it for duplicate evidence.

**Findings:** None.
